messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers: BAC ≥ 0.04 %.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations can lead to a $50 fine. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can result in a $50 fine. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Cannot pass the bus until it stops and the sign retracts. | Violations can lead to a $200 fine. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Illegal lane changes can result in a $50 fine. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid permit. | Failure to register can lead to a $200 fine. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green light = go; yellow light = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | Running a red light can result in a $200 fine. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance can lead to license suspension. | | **Special Zones** | • Construction zones: speed limit reduced by 10 mph.
• School zones: speed limit reduced by 10 mph during school hours. | Violations can lead to a $100 fine. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website provides statutes, regulations, and updates. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online; covers all traffic laws in detail. 3. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Offers driver’s handbook and licensing information. 4. **Legal Aid & Law Libraries** – For case law and interpretations of specific statutes. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular law or how to handle a specific traffic situation!
